sources.title: Exploiting parallel tool calls to make agentic search 4x faster
sources.evidence: Reopened in full from the October 27, 2026 fresh fetch. The December 8, 2025 launch describes on-policy RL, an unnamed base model, 8 H200 GPUs, three epochs on 3.2k examples and a separate search harness. It reports no nominal total or activated parameter count. Its numerical evaluation tables concern latency, accuracy and token usage, not model parameters; inspiration from SWE-grep does not identify a base checkpoint.

sources.title: Search Code
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Identifies relace-search as the language model behind FAS. Its chat-completions endpoint returns tool calls; callers execute them and append results. The Models table lists the model ID and tools, without total/active sizes or named-base lineage. Documents text messages and function arguments, but no numeric native context maximum. OpenAPI MIT metadata licenses the specification, not model weights.

sources.title: Fast Agentic Search: Overview
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Publishes the trained prompt and schemas for view_file, view_directory, grep_search, bash and report_back. Model-generated tool selections are distinct from backend execution. Describes the relace-search model and search harness separately, without a parameter count or named underlying checkpoint.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.evidence: Defines the company API as access to its auxiliary code models, grants limited service access, reserves proprietary rights, restricts distribution and reverse engineering, and states inference occurs on company systems.

sources.title: Relace Search: provider endpoints
sources.evidence: Relace-hosted relace-search-20251208 endpoint advertises context_length 256000 and max_completion_tokens 128000, text input/output and tool calling. This establishes hosting limits, not an independently disclosed architectural maximum.

sources.title: Relace Blog
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The research index still lists the original December 2025 FAS training article and the July 13, 2026 Compact release as the newer model research article. Followed and read that later original article (s9); it supplies no Search count or shared-base relationship.

sources.title: Relace complete documentation
sources.evidence: Reopened from the successful October 27, 2026 fresh fetch. Read the Search API/harness and model-catalog sections and searched the complete document for total/active counts and base-model names. Search, Apply, Compact and hosted open models remain separate. No Search parameter count or named-base lineage is given; the catalog describes prices, context, modalities and API request parameters, not neural parameter counts.

sources.title: Relace authenticated model catalog
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 401; no model-specific metadata was read from this endpoint.

sources.title: Relace Compact: 50k TPS for 50% cost savings
sources.evidence: Read in full from the October 27, 2026 fresh fetch. This July 13, 2026 original research/release article identifies Compact as a modified LLM for token-level classification and evaluates compaction speed and cost. It gives no Search total/active parameter count, no Search comparison parameter column and no named shared backbone from which Search size could be inherited.

name.note: Official product name and exact relace-search identifier.

family.note: No named underlying model lineage is disclosed; Search is a product name, not evidence of a shared backbone with Apply or Compact.

release_date.note: Dated announcement explicitly makes the model and API available that day; not inferred from provider listing time.

open_weights.note: Released as a proprietary hosted model. The accessed release and current documentation offer API access, without a weight distribution; public harness code does not distribute model weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification under the restricted hosted-service terms, not the MIT label on the API specification.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found neither a developer-published nominal total nor an explicitly named base model supporting a lineage inference. Reopened the full FAS training article, current Search API/harness, complete docs and later Compact article. Separate searches for Relace Search/relace-search/FAS total parameters, billion-scale size, Qwen/Llama base lineage and later research comparisons found no supported count. Training hardware, throughput, SWE-grep inspiration and other Relace products do not establish Search size.

active_parameters_b.note: Independently rechecked activated/active parameters on October 27. The original FAS evaluation tables contain latency, accuracy and token usage, not an active-parameter column; current docs and the later Compact research article add no Search count. Targeted active/activated-parameter and later original-paper searches found no usable exact-model comparison or named-base lineage. Parallel tool execution is unrelated to parameter activation; no dense-equals-active inference is made.

architecture.note: The base model is unnamed. RL, verl and the search harness do not establish Transformer, dense or MoE structure; no exact-model configuration or checkpoint was identified.

context_window.note: Documented maximum for the Relace-hosted relace-search-20251208 endpoint on OpenRouter, with128000 maximum completion tokens. This catalog field records available context, not a claim about native training length or architectural maximum. The direct Relace model catalog requires authentication; no inference request was made.

modalities.note: Model consumes text conversation/code/tool results and emits text/function arguments. Access to files through external tools adds no neural modality.

reasoning.note: Developer reports explicit reasoning steps emerging between tool-call bursts during RL and encourages reasoning in subsequent training. This does not imply a separate thinking-token API or adjustable reasoning budget.

tool_call.note: The model generates function calls for the documented search tools; the harness executes them. This is model tool selection, not merely an external agent invoking Search.

description.value: Code-search language model trained with reinforcement learning to select parallel file and grep tools, reason across search turns, and report relevant file ranges to a coding agent.
description.note: Replaces the generic chat description with the documented specialized task and model behavior; embedding retrieval and the managed harness are distinct components.

patch.description: Code-search language model trained with reinforcement learning to select parallel file and grep tools, reason across search turns, and report relevant file ranges to a coding agent.

sources.label: Exploiting parallel tool calls to make agentic search 4x faster
Relace Compact: 50k TPS for 50% cost savings

patch.notes: Relace Search is the separately callable RL-trained model behind Fast Agentic Search, distinct from embedding retrieval and the execution harness. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed; no named base model supports an inherited size. It emits reasoning and model-selected tool calls, without a separately documented thinking-token interface. OpenRouter advertises a 256,000-token Relace endpoint context and 128,000-token completion limit; native context and neural architecture remain undisclosed. SDK/harness and OpenAPI licenses are not model-weight licenses.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained undisclosed total and active counts after fresh original launch, Search API/harness, complete documentation and later Compact research checks, plus separate size, activation and named-base searches. No nominal count or supported lineage was found. The other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
